extracted.intended_audience: individuals seeking registration to practice before the USPTO and their counsel (petitioners to the USPTO Director; applicants affected by OED decisions)
extracted.subtask_description: Decision addressing a petition for waiver of the 60-day time limit to request review of an OED final decision and applying USPTO regulations on eligibility to register where an applicant has a criminal conviction and is on probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of request for review (37 C.F.R. § 11.2(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for review of the Final Decision of the OED Director will be dismissed as untimely unless it is filed within 60 days of the mailing date of the final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for review must be filed no later than the 60th day after mailing of the final decision (example: filing deadline here was August 17, 2009). A petitioner seeking more time must seek a waiver under the proper regulation (see § 11.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver authority for regulatory requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: In an extraordinary situation, when justice requires, any requirement of the regulations of this part ... may be suspended or waived by the USPTO Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain relief under § 11.3 a petitioner must demonstrate an 'extraordinary situation' such that 'justice requires' waiver of the applicable rule. Mere assertions or pending administrative actions (e.g., a provisional pardon application or a motion to terminate probation) are not automatically sufficient to meet this standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility to apply for registration during sentence/probation and for two years after (37 C.F.R. § 11.7(h)(1)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual who has been convicted of a ... misdemeanor ... shall not be eligible to apply for registration during the time of any sentence ... and period of probation ... and for a period of two years after completion of the sentence ... and period of probation ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant is currently serving probation (example: probation scheduled to end April 24, 2010), they are not eligible to apply until two years after probation ends (example: eligibility would begin April 24, 2012).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of provisional pardon on criminal record and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for the State of Connecticut Board of Pardons and Paroles Application indicate that a provisional pardon does not erase a criminal history; Conn. Gen. Stat. § 54-130e(g) indicates a provisional pardon is considered temporary any time the offender is on probation and the board can revoke it for a probation violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provisional pardon may not remove the disqualifying effect of a conviction for purposes of USPTO registration or accelerate eligibility; reliance on a provisional pardon pending final action is weak support for a § 11.3 waiver because it may be revocable and does not erase the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of probation does not eliminate two-year post-probation waiting period
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if a motion to terminate probation is granted, the two-year waiting period after the end of probation applies before an applicant becomes eligible under § 11.7(h)(1)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus, terminating probation would not, by itself, create immediate eligibility; obtaining the relief sought from the Director (e.g., registration despite the conviction) would require waiver of § 11.7(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility to apply precludes registration (interpretive/supporting authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: "[I]neligibility to apply for registration precludes registration." (69 FR 35428, 35431 (June 24, 2004)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an individual is ineligible to apply under the regulations, they cannot be registered; this regulatory principle supports denial of petitions that seek to circumvent eligibility rules without a proper waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper procedural route for extension requests concerning § 11.2(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for additional time to file a request for review of an OED final decision under 37 C.F.R. § 11.2(d) are governed by § 11.3 (waiver/suspension), not by 37 C.F.R. § 1.136(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners should invoke § 11.3 when seeking extra time to file a request for review under § 11.2(d); citing § 1.136(b) is not the applicable mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard applied in denying § 11.3 waiver requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director will deny a § 11.3 waiver where the petitioner has not shown a compelling case of an "extraordinary situation" such that justice requires suspension or waiver of the regulation at issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this decision, the Director found no compelling case because even if the petitioner obtained a provisional pardon or probation termination, statutory/regulatory time bars (and provisional nature of the pardon) meant the requested relief could not be obtained through review; therefore, waiver was inappropriate.
